s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with peritonism and sepsis
salient_findings: Multi-organ involvement with lymphadenopathy and pulmonary consolidation
key_facts: 60-year-old man with history of heavy cigarette smoking
History of emphysema, hypertension, and prostate cancer in remission
4-hour history of acute right lower-quadrant abdominal pain
Fever of 38.5°C on admission
Hypotension with systolic blood pressure 90 mmHg
Tachycardia with heart rate 110/min
Peritonism in the right lower quadrant
Perforated appendix on CT scan
Collection and surrounding fat stranding on CT scan
Innumerable hepatic nodules on CT scan
Mural thickening of the cecum and sigmoid colon on CT scan
Lymphadenopathy on CT scan
Pulmonary consolidation and collapse on CT scan
Subtotal colectomy with end ileostomy performed

shortlist.label: Acute appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: Perforated appendix on CT scan and peritonism

shortlist.label: Peritonitis
shortlist.why_kept: Peritonism and purulent contamination during surgery

shortlist.label: Sepsis
shortlist.why_kept: Fever, hypotension, and tachycardia on admission

shortlist.label: Colorectal cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Thickened, woody sigmoid colon and innumerable hepatic nodules on CT scan

shortlist.label: Sepsis-induced multi-organ failure
shortlist.why_kept: Multi-organ involvement and failure to recover postoperatively

raw.rationale: The patient presented with fever, hypotension, and tachycardia, which are classic signs of sepsis, and the CT scan showed a perforated appendix, which is a common cause of sepsis. The patient's rapid deterioration and multi-organ failure also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Acute appendicitis
rejected.why: While the patient had a perforated appendix, this is more of a contributing factor to the sepsis rather than the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Peritonitis
rejected.why: Peritonitis is a complication of the perforated appendix, but it does not fully explain the patient's systemic symptoms and multi-organ failure.

rejected.label: Colorectal cancer
rejected.why: Although the patient had a history of prostate cancer and the CT scan showed mural thickening of the cecum and sigmoid colon, there is not enough evidence to suggest that colorectal cancer is the primary cause of the patient's current condition.

rejected.label: Sepsis-induced multi-organ failure
rejected.why: This is a consequence of sepsis, rather than a separate diagnosis. The patient's condition is best explained by sepsis, which led to multi-organ failure.
